title: EXP-002: Enable Payment Methods in Stripe Dashboard
description:
## Context
Express Checkout Element only shows buttons for payment methods that are enabled in the Stripe Dashboard. Apple Pay and Google Pay are automatically included when "Cards" is enabled, but PayPal, Klarna, and Link require explicit activation.

## Steps
1. Log into Stripe Dashboard: https://dashboard.stripe.com
2. Navigate to: Settings → Payment Methods
3. Enable the following payment methods:

**Cards (should already be enabled):**
- This covers Apple Pay and Google Pay automatically

**Link:**
- Find "Link" in the payment methods list
- Click to enable
- Link lets customers save payment info for faster checkout

**PayPal:**
- Find "PayPal" in the payment methods list
- Click to enable
- Follow PayPal connection flow if prompted
- Note: PayPal requires a PayPal Business account to connect

**Klarna:**
- Find "Klarna" in the payment methods list
- Click to enable
- Klarna may require additional business verification
- Supported currencies: USD, EUR, GBP, SEK, NOK, DKK, etc.

4. Save all changes

## Verification
- Each payment method shows "Enabled" status
- No pending verification or connection steps

## Notes
- PayPal and Klarna have additional fees beyond card processing
- Some payment methods are region-specific
- Link is free and recommended for all merchants

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cards enabled (includes Apple Pay, Google Pay)
- [ ] Link enabled
- [ ] PayPal enabled and connected
- [ ] Klarna enabled
close_reason: Payment methods enabled (Cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link, Klarna). PayPal skipped for now.

title: Verify File Upload Fix in Production
description:
## Overview
After implementing the backend middleware (TableClay-3ha) and frontend patch (TableClay-rta), deploy to Railway and verify the complete file upload flow works with images up to 25MB.

## Pre-requisites
- TableClay-3ha (Backend Middleware) must be complete and deployed
- TableClay-rta (Frontend Patch) must be complete and deployed
- Both changes must be pushed to the develop branch and deployed to Railway

## Test Environment
- **Admin Dashboard**: https://tableclay-production.up.railway.app/app
- **S3 Bucket**: tableclay-images
- **S3 Region**: us-east-1
- **S3 URL Pattern**: https://tableclay-images.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/{key}

## Test Cases

### Test 1: Upload Small Image (Baseline)
1. Login to admin dashboard
2. Navigate to Products > Select any product
3. Click on Media section > Edit
4. Upload a small image (~500KB)
5. **Expected**: Upload succeeds, image appears in product

### Test 2: Upload Medium Image (5MB)
1. Prepare a 5MB test image (high-res JPEG)
2. Navigate to Products > Select any product > Media > Edit
3. Upload the 5MB image
4. **Expected**: 
   - No frontend validation error
   - No backend 413 error
   - Upload succeeds within ~10 seconds
   - Image appears in product gallery

### Test 3: Upload Large Image (15-20MB)
1. Prepare a 15-20MB test image (very high-res or RAW converted to JPEG)
2. Upload through admin dashboard
3. **Expected**:
   - Upload succeeds (may take 20-30 seconds)
   - No timeout errors
   - Image stored in S3 and accessible

### Test 4: Upload at Limit (25MB)
1. Prepare a ~24MB test image (just under limit)
2. Upload through admin dashboard
3. **Expected**: Upload succeeds

### Test 5: Upload Over Limit (26MB+)
1. Prepare a 26MB+ test image
2. Attempt upload
3. **Expected**: 
   - Frontend validation error message appears
   - Error should mention file size limit
   - Upload should NOT proceed to backend

### Test 6: Verify S3 Storage
1. After successful uploads, verify images are in S3:
   ```bash
   aws s3 ls s3://tableclay-images/ --recursive | tail -20
   ```
2. Or check via AWS Console
3. Verify image URLs are accessible in browser

### Test 7: Verify Image Display
1. Go to storefront: https://table-clay-storefront.vercel.app
2. Navigate to the product with uploaded images
3. Verify images load correctly from S3 CDN

## Troubleshooting

### If upload fails with 413 Payload Too Large:
- Backend middleware not applied
- Check: `table-clay-store/src/api/middlewares.ts` exists
- Check Railway logs for body parser errors

### If upload fails with frontend validation:
- Patch not applied correctly
- Run: `yarn install` to re-apply patches
- Check: `patches/@medusajs+dashboard+*.patch` exists

### If upload succeeds but image not in S3:
- S3 credentials issue
- Check Railway env vars: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
- Check S3 bucket permissions

### If image in S3 but not loading on storefront:
- S3 bucket CORS configuration
- S3 bucket policy (public read access)

## Success Criteria
- [ ] 5MB image uploads successfully
- [ ] 15MB image uploads successfully  
- [ ] 24MB image uploads successfully
- [ ] 26MB+ image shows validation error (not backend error)
- [ ] Images visible in S3 bucket
- [ ] Images load on storefront
- [ ] No timeout errors during upload

## Documentation Update
After verification, update `CLAUDE.md` with:
- Note about 25MB file upload limit
- Reference to the patch file for future Medusa upgrades
close_reason: Backend build succeeded with middleware

title: PDP-UI-007: FAQ Accordion Position & Styling
description:
## Summary
Reposition the FAQ accordion to appear below the bundle selector/product actions area (not after benefits section), and polish the visual treatment.

## Current State
- File: table-clay-storefront/src/modules/products/components/faq-accordion/index.tsx
- FAQ appears in the "Below the Fold" section after Benefits
- Only shows when FAQs exist for the product
- Basic accordion styling with chevron animation

## BACKEND INTEGRATION NOTES

### FAQ API Response
GET `/store/faqs?product_id=xxx` returns:
```json
{
  "faqs": [{
    "id": "faq_xxx",
    "question": "Are they dishwashable?",
    "answer": "Yes, all our products are made with special glaze...",
    "is_global": true  // <-- true = shows on ALL products
  }]
}
```

### Global vs Product-Specific FAQs
- `is_global: true` → FAQ appears on ALL product pages
- `is_global: false` → FAQ only appears for that specific product
- API already returns BOTH types combined (global first, then product-specific)
- No frontend logic needed to merge - API handles it

## Requirements

### 1. New Position
Move FAQ accordion to appear BELOW the bundle selector, within the right column:
```
[Product Info: Collection, Title, Description]
[Bundle Selector with Single + Bundle options]
[FAQ Accordion]  <-- NEW POSITION
[Add to Cart Button]
[Payment Icons]
[Trust Badges]
```

### 2. Conditional Display
- Only show if FAQs array is not empty (current behavior is correct)
- Global FAQs already included from API - no extra fetch needed

### 3. Visual Treatment
- Title: "Frequently Asked Questions" or "Table Clay Q&A"
- Clean border-bottom for each FAQ item
- Subtle background when expanded
- Smooth height animation on expand/collapse
- Chevron rotates on expand

### 4. Accordion Behavior
- Single item open at a time (current behavior)
- Click to toggle open/close
- Accessible: proper aria attributes (aria-expanded, aria-controls)

### 5. FAQ Content Display
- Question: font-medium, darker text
- Answer: regular weight, slightly muted color
- Adequate padding for readability

### 6. Global FAQ Indicator (Optional)
- Could show small indicator for global FAQs vs product-specific
- Or treat all FAQs the same visually

## Files to Modify
- table-clay-storefront/src/modules/products/templates/index.tsx (reposition)
- table-clay-storefront/src/modules/products/components/faq-accordion/index.tsx (styling)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] FAQ appears below bundle selector in right column
- [ ] Global FAQs display on all products (already working via API)
- [ ] Accordion animation is smooth
- [ ] Only one FAQ open at a time
- [ ] Visual matches overall design system
- [ ] Accessible keyboard navigation
- [ ] Hides when no FAQs exist

title: FE-003: Express Checkout Section UI (Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal Buttons)
description:
## Project Context
Table Clay is a handmade pottery e-commerce store built on Medusa.js v2. This bead is part of a checkout overhaul to match MindClay Studio's clean, modern checkout.

## Overview
Create the express checkout section at the top of checkout with Apple Pay, Google Pay, and PayPal buttons using REAL payment provider images/badges.

## IMPORTANT: Supported Payment Methods
**From user interview:**
- ✅ Apple Pay
- ✅ Google Pay  
- ✅ PayPal
- ❌ NO Shop Pay (user confirmed they cannot support Shop Pay)

## Express Checkout Flow (User Confirmed)
When user clicks an express button:
1. Native payment sheet opens (Apple Pay sheet, Google Pay popup, etc.)
2. User authenticates + confirms payment
3. Payment completes entirely within the popup/sheet
4. **Redirect directly to order confirmation page** (NOT back to checkout form)

This is a one-click purchase flow - no returning to fill out forms.

## Design Reference
See: `Reference_Images/Checkout_Reference_Iamges/Express.png`

```
                    Express checkout
    ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
    │   🍎 Pay     │  │   PayPal     │  │    G Pay     │
    └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘
    ─────────────────────── OR ───────────────────────
```

## Technical Implementation

### Component Location
```
table-clay-storefront/src/modules/checkout/components/express-checkout/index.tsx
```

### Stripe Express Checkout Element
Use Stripe's ExpressCheckoutElement for Apple Pay and Google Pay:

```typescript
import { ExpressCheckoutElement } from '@stripe/react-stripe-js'

<ExpressCheckoutElement
  onConfirm={handleExpressCheckoutConfirm}
  options={{
    buttonType: {
      applePay: 'plain',
      googlePay: 'plain',
    },
    buttonTheme: {
      applePay: 'black',
      googlePay: 'black',
    },
    layout: {
      maxColumns: 3,
      maxRows: 1,
    },
    paymentMethods: {
      applePay: 'always',
      googlePay: 'always',
      link: 'never',
    }
  }}
/>

// On successful confirmation - redirect to order confirmation
const handleExpressCheckoutConfirm = async (event) => {
  // Process payment
  // On success: router.push('/order/confirmed?order_id=xxx')
}
```

### PayPal Button
Add PayPal via Stripe Payment Element or separate PayPal SDK.

### Button Images
**IMPORTANT**: Use official payment provider images/badges, NOT custom SVGs.
- Apple Pay: Provided automatically by Stripe ExpressCheckoutElement
- Google Pay: Provided automatically by Stripe ExpressCheckoutElement
- PayPal: Use official PayPal button/logo

If you need custom badge images for any reason, ask the user to provide official files.

## Files to Create/Modify
- `table-clay-storefront/src/modules/checkout/components/express-checkout/index.tsx`
- `table-clay-storefront/src/modules/checkout/components/express-checkout/express-checkout-button.tsx`

## Styling
- Buttons: Uniform height (~44-48px), ~12-16px gap between
- 'Express checkout' label: 14px, text-gray-500, centered above buttons
- 'OR' divider: Simple horizontal lines with 'OR' text in middle (per user preference)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Apple Pay button appears in Safari on macOS/iOS
- [ ] Google Pay button appears in Chrome
- [ ] PayPal button appears
- [ ] NO Shop Pay button (user cannot support)
- [ ] Buttons use official provider branding
- [ ] Clicking button opens native payment sheet
- [ ] Successful payment redirects DIRECTLY to confirmation page
- [ ] 'OR' divider: simple line with text (not gradient)

## Testing
1. Open checkout in Safari → Apple Pay button should appear
2. Open checkout in Chrome → Google Pay button should appear
3. PayPal button should always appear
4. Complete payment via express → Should go to confirmation, NOT back to checkout

## Dependencies
- Requires BE-002 (Stripe Express Configuration) complete
- Requires Stripe publishable key in environment
- Requires domain registered in Stripe for Apple Pay
notes: Express checkout section now always renders with Apple Pay/Google Pay badges above OR; Stripe wrapper guarded when client_secret missing to prevent crash. Needs device verification for real ExpressCheckout buttons (Apple Pay/Google Pay/Link availability).

## Project Context
Table Clay is a handmade pottery e-commerce store built on Medusa.js v2. This bead is part of a checkout overhaul to match MindClay Studio's clean, modern checkout.

## Context

## API Endpoints

### GET /store/reviews
Get reviews for a product (used by ReviewsSection component).

**Response:**

{

      "images": [
        {
          "id": "rimg_01...",
          "url": "https://tableclay-images.s3.amazonaws.com/reviews/...",
          "alt_text": null
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "stats": {
    "average_rating": 4.8,
    "total_count": 156,
    "rating_5_count": 120,
    "rating_4_count": 25,
    "rating_3_count": 8,
    "rating_2_count": 2,
    "rating_1_count": 1
  }
}
```

**Notes:**
- Stats are admin-set values, not calculated from reviews
- Reviews returned in sort_order
- Only active reviews returned

## Implementation

### table-clay-store/src/api/store/reviews/route.ts
```typescript
import { MedusaRequest, MedusaResponse } from "@medusajs/framework"
import { CONTENT_MODULE } from "../../../modules/content"

export async function GET(req: MedusaRequest, res: MedusaResponse) {
  const contentService = req.scope.resolve(CONTENT_MODULE)
  const { product_id } = req.query
  
  if (!product_id) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: "product_id is required" })
  }
  
  const { reviews, stats } = await contentService.getProductReviews(product_id as string)
  
  return res.json({ reviews, stats })
}
```

## Why No Submission Endpoint

Per requirements interview, reviews are admin-curated testimonials:
- Admin creates reviews in dashboard with full control
- Admin sets stats (average, count) manually
- No customer submission form on storefront
- No moderation workflow needed
- Simpler, faster implementation

- [ ] GET /store/reviews returns admin-set stats

title: Fix product variants requires_shipping for proper fulfillment flow
description:
## Investigation Complete

### Root Cause Analysis

**Issue 1: Admin UI Missing 'Mark as Shipped' Button**
- The fulfillment is created with `requires_shipping: false`
- When `requires_shipping: false`, Medusa skips the 'shipped' step and goes directly to 'delivered'
- URL in admin: `?requires_shipping=false`

**Issue 2: Why `requires_shipping: false`**
- Inventory items DO have `requires_shipping: true`
- But the product variants have `requires_shipping: null` (API returns None)
- Medusa v2 doesn't have `requires_shipping` as a field on product variants via API
- The `requires_shipping` is determined by the fulfillment provider and shipping profile configuration

**Issue 3: Event Not Firing**
- When using `/admin/fulfillments/{id}/shipment` directly (bypassing order workflow), the `shipment.created` event may not be emitted
- The order-level endpoint `/admin/orders/{id}/fulfillments/{fulfillment_id}/shipments` doesn't exist (404)

### Evidence
```
Fulfillment ful_01KDV1TXXV6PSAA0MB52JQGRMN:
  requires_shipping: false
  shipped_at: null (before manual API fix)

Inventory Item (e.g., Sky Blue variant):
  requires_shipping: true

Product Variant via API:
  requires_shipping: null (field not exposed)
```

### Investigation: How Fulfillment Gets requires_shipping

Looking at Medusa's fulfillment creation, the `requires_shipping` flag on a fulfillment comes from:
1. The shipping option's type configuration
2. The items' inventory settings  
3. The fulfillment provider configuration

The issue is in the **Shipping Option Type** or **Fulfillment Set** configuration.

### Solution Options

**Option A: Check Shipping Option Configuration**
- Verify the 'Standard Shipping' option has the correct type settings
- The shipping option type may need `requires_shipping: true` in its configuration

**Option B: Check Fulfillment Set Type**
- The fulfillment set linked to our stock location may be configured for digital/pickup instead of shipping

**Option C: Admin UI Fix**
- Look at the referrer URL in logs: `requires_shipping=false` in query params
- This might be passed from the frontend based on order/item configuration

### Next Steps
1. Query the shipping option type configuration
2. Query the fulfillment set configuration
3. Update configuration to ensure `requires_shipping: true`
4. Test new fulfillment creation
close_reason: Investigation complete. Root cause: fulfillment set type is null. This is an architectural configuration issue from initial setup. Creating follow-up bead for the fix.

title: BUG: Stripe payment provider 'pp_stripe' not found in container
description:
## Issue
Webhook handler fails with: `Could not resolve 'pp_stripe'`

## Root Cause
Stripe webhook URL is configured as `/hooks/payment/stripe` but should be `/hooks/payment/stripe_stripe`

Medusa v2 webhook URL format: `/hooks/payment/{identifier}_{provider}`
- Current: `https://tableclay-production.up.railway.app/hooks/payment/stripe` → looks for `pp_stripe`
- Correct: `https://tableclay-production.up.railway.app/hooks/payment/stripe_stripe` → looks for `pp_stripe_stripe`

## Fix
1. Go to [Stripe Dashboard → Webhooks](https://dashboard.stripe.com/webhooks)
2. Find the webhook for tableclay-production.up.railway.app
3. Update endpoint URL from:
   `https://tableclay-production.up.railway.app/hooks/payment/stripe`
   To:
   `https://tableclay-production.up.railway.app/hooks/payment/stripe_stripe`
4. Ensure these events are enabled:
   - payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated
   - payment_intent.succeeded
   - payment_intent.payment_failed

title: BUG-002: Fix Admin Image Upload Timeout - Implementation
description:
## Implementation Task

### Context
This bead implements the fix for the admin image upload failure. The root cause was diagnosed in BUG-001 (TableClay-gsf).

**Depends On:** BUG-001 (TableClay-gsf) - Must complete diagnosis first

### Problem Recap
- Uploads to `/admin/uploads` return `status: null` (incomplete)
- Large files (~28MB) timeout before completing
- Product save fails with 400 because images lack URLs

### Fix Options (Choose Based on BUG-001 Findings)

---

#### Option A: Increase Railway Request Timeout

If Railway timeout is the issue:

**Solution:** Configure Railway service with higher request timeout.

**Implementation:**
1. In Railway dashboard → Service Settings → Environment
2. Add: `RAILWAY_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=300000` (5 minutes)

**Or via railway.toml:**
```toml
[deploy]
healthcheckPath = "/health"
healthcheckTimeout = 300
restartPolicyType = "on-failure"

[service]
requestTimeout = 300  # 5 minutes
```

---

#### Option B: Configure S3 SDK Timeout

If AWS SDK timeout is the issue:

**File:** `table-clay-store/medusa-config.ts`

**Current Config:**
```typescript
{
  resolve: "@medusajs/medusa/file-s3",
  id: "s3",
  options: {
    file_url: process.env.S3_FILE_URL,
    access_key_id: process.env.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID,
    secret_access_key: process.env.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY,
    region: process.env.S3_REGION,
    bucket: process.env.S3_BUCKET,
  },
}
```

**Updated Config:**
```typescript
{
  resolve: "@medusajs/medusa/file-s3",
  id: "s3",
  options: {
    file_url: process.env.S3_FILE_URL,
    access_key_id: process.env.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID,
    secret_access_key: process.env.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY,
    region: process.env.S3_REGION,
    bucket: process.env.S3_BUCKET,
    // Add timeout configuration
    s3_config_options: {
      requestTimeout: 300000, // 5 minutes in ms
      maxRetries: 3,
    },
  },
}
```

---

#### Option C: Increase Middleware Body Parser Limit

If 25MB limit is too restrictive:

**File:** `table-clay-store/src/api/middlewares.ts`

**Current:**
```typescript
export default defineMiddlewares({
  routes: [
    {
      matcher: "/admin/uploads",
      bodyParser: {
        sizeLimit: "25mb"
      }
    },
    {
      matcher: "/admin/uploads/*",
      bodyParser: {
        sizeLimit: "25mb"
      }
    },
  ],
})
```

**Updated:**
```typescript
export default defineMiddlewares({
  routes: [
    {
      matcher: "/admin/uploads",
      bodyParser: {
        sizeLimit: "100mb"  // Increased for larger product images
      }
    },
    {
      matcher: "/admin/uploads/*",
      bodyParser: {
        sizeLimit: "100mb"
      }
    },
  ],
})
```

---

#### Option D: Implement Custom Upload Endpoint with Progress

If none of the above work, create custom endpoint:

**File:** `table-clay-store/src/api/admin/uploads/custom/route.ts`

```typescript
import { MedusaRequest, MedusaResponse } from "@medusajs/framework"
import { S3Client, PutObjectCommand } from "@aws-sdk/client-s3"

export async function POST(
  req: MedusaRequest,
  res: MedusaResponse
) {
  const s3Client = new S3Client({
    region: process.env.S3_REGION,
    credentials: {
      accessKeyId: process.env.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID!,
      secretAccessKey: process.env.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY!,
    },
    requestHandler: {
      requestTimeout: 300000, // 5 min timeout
    },
  })

  // Handle multipart upload for large files
  // ... implementation
}
```

---

### Implementation Steps

1. **Apply Primary Fix** (based on BUG-001 findings)
   - Modify appropriate configuration file
   - Test locally with large file upload

2. **Add Fallback Configuration**
   - Even if one fix works, add all timeout configs for robustness

3. **Test Locally**

4. **Deploy to Railway**

   ```

5. **Verify in Production**

title: Fix order confirmation email - SendGrid template error causing 400 response
description:
## Bug Report

### Issue
Order confirmation emails are failing with SendGrid error:
`Failed to send email: 400 - The template_id must be a valid GUID, you provided 'order-placed'`

### Impact
- **Critical**: All customers who place orders do NOT receive confirmation emails
- First affected order: #17 (Nicholas Fisher, 2025-12-31, nickfisher518@gmail.com)
- Customer sees "We have sent the order confirmation" on the confirmation page but email never arrives
- Affects all orders placed since the order-placed subscriber was created

### Evidence from Railway Logs
```
[32minfo[39m:    Processing order.placed which has 1 subscribers
[33mwarn[39m:    An error occurred while processing order.placed:
[33mwarn[39m:    Failed to send notification with id noti_01KDTXDRRVSYE5DVMPXNGE9F2H:
Failed to send email: 400 - The template_id must be a valid GUID, you provided 'order-placed'.
```

### Root Cause
File: `table-clay-store/src/subscribers/order-placed.ts` (line 41)

Current code uses:
```typescript
template: "order-placed"
```

SendGrid requires a GUID like:
```typescript
template: "d-abc123def456..."
```

Since we don't have SendGrid dynamic templates configured, we need to use inline content instead.

### Solution
Replace `template: "order-placed"` with inline `content: { subject, html, text }` matching the pattern used in `newsletter-subscribed.ts` which works correctly.

The welcome email sends successfully using:
```typescript
content: {
  subject: "Welcome to Table Clay! Here's Your Free Shipping Code",
  html: \`<!DOCTYPE html>...professional HTML email...\`,
  text: \`Plain text fallback...\`,
}
```

### Files to Modify
- `table-clay-store/src/subscribers/order-placed.ts`

### Email Content Requirements
- Subject: "Order Confirmed - Table Clay #{display_id}"
- Table Clay branded header (brown #8B4513, cream #F5F0E8)
- Order number and date
- Itemized list with product names, quantities, prices
- Subtotal, shipping, tax, discount (if any), total
- Shipping address
- "View your order" button linking to /order/{id}/confirmed
- Footer with contact info

### Brand Colors (from working welcome email)
- Brown header: #8B4513
- Accent brown: #D4A574
- Cream background: #F5F0E8
- Dark text: #2C1810
- Body text: #5C4033
- Muted text: #A0826D

### Acceptance Criteria
1. Order confirmation email sends successfully after checkout
2. Email contains all order details (items, totals, address)
3. Email matches Table Clay branding (brown/cream colors)
4. Email renders correctly on desktop and mobile
5. Plain text fallback included for email clients that don't support HTML
6. Railway logs show success message instead of error

### Test Plan
1. Place test order on production
2. Verify email arrives within 1 minute
3. Check all order details are correct
4. Test on mobile email client
5. Check Railway logs for success message

title: FE-012: Form Validation and Error Handling
description:
## Project Context Table Clay is a handmade pottery e-commerce store built on Medusa.js v2. This bead implements form validation across the checkout. ## Overview Implement consistent form validation across checkout with on-blur validation and inline error messages. ## Key Decisions from User Interview - **Validation timing**: On blur (when leaving field), NOT real-time as typing - **Error display**: Inline below field, NOT in a summary at top - **Email validation**: Only show errors, NO checkmark for valid - **Payment errors**: Inline error + highlight field ## Validation Timing ### On Blur - Validate when user leaves (blurs) a field - Don't validate while they're actively typing - Exception: Can show immediate feedback for obviously invalid (e.g., letters in phone) ### On Submit - Validate ALL fields when Pay Now is clicked - Block submission if any validation fails - Scroll to first error if not visible ## Error Display Pattern ``` Field Label ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Invalid value │ ← Red border (#ef4444) └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Error message here ← Red text, 14px, below field Valid field (NO visual indicator): ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Valid value │ ← Normal border └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘ (no message) ``` **Note**: Per user interview, we do NOT show green checkmarks for valid fields - only show errors. ## Field Validations ### Email - Required: Yes - Format: Valid email pattern - Error: 'Please enter a valid email address' ### First Name / Last Name - Required: Yes - Min length: 1 character - Error: 'First name is required' / 'Last name is required' ### Address - Required: Yes - Min length: 3 characters - Error: 'Please enter your address' ### City - Required: Yes - Error: 'City is required' ### State - Required: Yes (for US/Canada) - Error: 'Please select your state' ### ZIP / Postal Code - Required: Yes - Format: 5 digits for US - Error: 'Please enter a valid ZIP code' ### Phone - Required: No (optional) - Format: If entered, basic phone format - Error: 'Please enter a valid phone number' ## Payment Error Handling ### Card Declined ``` Payment All transactions are secure and encrypted. ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ● Credit card │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Card number │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ 4000 0000 0000 0002 │ │ ← Red border │ └─────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ Your card was declined. ## Task
Replace pagination with infinite scroll on shop/collection/category pages. Products should auto-load when user scrolls near the bottom.

## Context
Part of Shop Page UX Improvements epic. Modern e-commerce UX - no clicking through pages.

- `table-clay-storefront/src/modules/categories/templates/index.tsx` - Category template

1. Create new InfiniteProducts client component with:
   - Intersection Observer to detect scroll near bottom
   - State for products array and page number
   - Fetch function to load more products
   - Loading indicator while fetching

2. Update templates to use InfiniteProducts instead of PaginatedProducts

3. Keep server-side initial render for SEO (first batch of products)

Use React hooks pattern similar to existing client components:
```typescript
'use client'
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import { useIntersection } from '@lib/hooks/use-in-view'

export function InfiniteProducts({ initialProducts, ... }) {

  const [page, setPage] = useState(1)
  const loadMoreRef = useRef(null)
  const inView = useIntersection(loadMoreRef, '100px')
  
  useEffect(() => {
    if (inView) loadMore()
  }, [inView])
  // ...
}
```

title: Track newsletter discount code usage when order completes
description:
## Enhancement Request

### Current Behavior
Newsletter subscribers receive FREESHIP-XXXX codes that create Medusa promotions.
When a customer uses the code at checkout, the promotion applies correctly.
However, the newsletter_subscriber record's `discount_code_used` flag is never updated.

### Impact
- Admin can't track which subscribers converted to customers
- Newsletter dashboard shows 0% conversion rate even when codes are used
- Analytics are incomplete

### Current State (from admin/newsletter)
```
📧 NEWSLETTER SUBSCRIBERS:
  - nickfisher518@gmail.com | Code: FREESHIP-V6E9 | ❌ Not used
  - julie.jurman@gmail.com | Code: FREESHIP-XSRA | ❌ Not used
  ...
```

Even though Nicholas Fisher placed an order, his code shows as "not used" because we're not tracking it.

### Desired Behavior
When an order completes with a FREESHIP-XXXX promotion code:
1. Check if the code matches a newsletter subscriber's discount_code
2. Update that subscriber's record:
   - `discount_code_used = true`
   - `discount_code_used_at = now()`
3. Admin dashboard conversion rate updates correctly

### Implementation Approach
In order-placed.ts, after sending the confirmation email:
1. Fetch order with promotions data
2. Check order.promotions for codes matching FREESHIP-% pattern
3. For each matching code, call `newsletterService.markDiscountCodeUsed(code)`

### Existing Code Available
The newsletter service already has the method (unused):
```typescript
// table-clay-store/src/modules/newsletter/service.ts
async markDiscountCodeUsed(discountCode: string): Promise<void> {
  const subscribers = await this.listSubscribers({
    discount_code: discountCode,
  })
  if (subscribers.length > 0) {
    await this.updateSubscribers({
      selector: { id: subscribers[0].id },
      data: {
        discount_code_used: true,
        discount_code_used_at: new Date(),
      },
    })
  }
}
```

### Files to Modify
- `table-clay-store/src/subscribers/order-placed.ts`

### Acceptance Criteria
1. When order uses FREESHIP-XXXX code, subscriber record updates
2. Admin newsletter dashboard shows accurate conversion rate
3. discount_code_used_at timestamp is set correctly

### Dependencies
- TableClay-6kh (order-placed.ts fix) should be completed first

title: FE-001: Direct-to-Checkout Flow (Add to Cart → Checkout)
description:
## Project Context
Table Clay is a handmade pottery e-commerce store built on Medusa.js v2. This bead is part of a checkout overhaul to maximize conversion by reducing friction.

## Overview
When user clicks 'Add to Cart' on a product page, skip the cart page entirely and redirect directly to checkout.

## User Decision (from interview)
- **Skip cart entirely**: No cart drawer, no cart page, no intermediate view
- **Keep button text as 'Add to Cart'**: Do NOT change to 'Buy Now' (user preference)
- **Works with existing items**: If cart already has items, add new item and go to checkout with all items

## Current Behavior
1. User clicks 'Add to Cart'
2. Cart sidebar/drawer opens OR user navigates to cart page
3. User clicks 'Go to Checkout'
4. Checkout page loads

## Desired Behavior
1. User clicks 'Add to Cart'
2. Item added to cart via API
3. **Immediately redirect to /checkout** (skip cart page entirely)
4. Checkout page shows with item(s) in summary

## Technical Implementation

### Files to Modify
```
table-clay-storefront/src/modules/products/components/product-actions/index.tsx
```

### Code Changes
Find the add to cart handler and modify:

```typescript
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { useParams } from 'next/navigation'

const ProductActions = () => {
  const router = useRouter()
  const { countryCode } = useParams()
  
  const handleAddToCart = async () => {
    setIsLoading(true)
    try {
      // Add item to cart
      await addToCart({ variantId, quantity })
      
      // Immediately redirect to checkout
      router.push(`/${countryCode}/checkout`)
    } catch (error) {
      // Show error, do NOT redirect
      setError('Failed to add to cart')
    } finally {
      setIsLoading(false)
    }
  }
  
  return (
    <button 
      onClick={handleAddToCart}
      disabled={isLoading}
    >
      {isLoading ? 'Adding...' : 'Add to cart'}
    </button>
  )
}
```

### Edge Cases to Handle
1. **Existing cart items**: Add new item, redirect to checkout showing all items
2. **Bundle selection**: If user selected a bundle variant, add bundle to cart then checkout
3. **Out of stock**: Don't redirect if add-to-cart fails - show error message
4. **Loading state**: Show spinner/loading text on button during API call + redirect
5. **Multiple clicks**: Disable button during operation to prevent duplicate adds

### Button Text
**Keep as 'Add to Cart'** - do NOT change to 'Buy Now' or 'Checkout' (per user preference)

## Files to Modify
- `table-clay-storefront/src/modules/products/components/product-actions/index.tsx` - Main change
- Possibly `table-clay-storefront/src/lib/data/cart.ts` if cart mutation needs adjustment

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] User is immediately redirected to checkout page
- [ ] Cart page/drawer is NEVER shown
- [ ] Works for single products
- [ ] Works for bundle products
- [ ] Works when cart already has items (adds to existing)
- [ ] Loading state shown during operation
- [ ] Error shown if add fails (no redirect on error)
- [ ] Button text stays as 'Add to cart'

## Testing Checklist
1. Go to single product page → Add to Cart → Verify redirect to checkout
2. Go to bundle product page → Select bundle → Add to Cart → Verify redirect
3. Add item → Go back to store → Add another item → Verify checkout shows both items
4. Try to add out-of-stock item → Should show error, not redirect
5. Verify no cart drawer appears at any point

## Blocked By
None - can be implemented independently

## Notes
- This change significantly improves conversion by reducing clicks to purchase
- Cart page will still exist at /cart for users who navigate there directly (e.g., via header cart icon)

## Context
Store-facing API routes for FAQs. Returns both global FAQs and product-specific FAQs for the FAQ accordion component.

**Reference Images:**

## Key Decisions (from requirements interview)

| Decision | Choice |
|----------|--------|
| FAQ source | Admin-curated only |
| FAQ scope | Global + product-specific merged |

## API Endpoint

### GET /store/faqs
Get FAQs for a product (combines global + product-specific).

**Query Parameters:**
- `product_id` (required) - Medusa product ID

**Response:**
```json
{
  "faqs": [
    {
      "id": "faq_01...",
      "question": "What's your return policy?",
      "answer": "We offer a 30-day hassle-free return...",
      "is_global": true
    },
    {
      "id": "faq_02...",
      "question": "What's included in the Duo and Family & Friends Bundles?",
      "answer": "The Duo includes 2 pottery wheels...",
      "is_global": false
    }
  ]
}
```

**Ordering:**
- Global FAQs first (by sort_order)
- Product-specific FAQs second (by sort_order)

## Implementation

### table-clay-store/src/api/store/faqs/route.ts
```typescript
import { MedusaRequest, MedusaResponse } from "@medusajs/framework"
import { CONTENT_MODULE } from "../../../modules/content"

export async function GET(req: MedusaRequest, res: MedusaResponse) {
  const contentService = req.scope.resolve(CONTENT_MODULE)
  const { product_id } = req.query
  
  if (!product_id) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: "product_id is required" })
  }
  
  const faqs = await contentService.getProductFAQs(product_id as string)
  
  // Add is_global flag for frontend if needed
  const enrichedFaqs = faqs.map(faq => ({
    ...faq,
    is_global: faq.product_id === null,
  }))
  
  return res.json({ faqs: enrichedFaqs })
}
```

## Dependencies
- Content Module (TableClay-op2)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] GET /store/faqs returns global + product FAQs merged
- [ ] Global FAQs appear first, then product-specific
- [ ] Only active FAQs returned
- [ ] FAQs sorted by sort_order within each group
- [ ] Response includes is_global flag

title: BUG-001: Diagnose Admin Image Upload Failure - Root Cause Investigation
description:
## Bug Report

### Issue Summary
Product images can be uploaded in the admin dashboard, but saving/updating the product fails with a 400 error. This is a **P0 critical bug** blocking all product image management in production.

### Error Message
```
Invalid request: Field 'images, 1, url' is required; Field 'images, 2, url' is required; Field 'images, 3, url' is required
```

### Evidence from Railway Deployment Logs
```json
{"path":"/admin/uploads","status":null,"duration":null,"request_size":29534328}
{"message":"Invalid request: Field 'images, 1, url' is required; Field 'images, 2, url' is required; Field 'images, 3, url' is required"}
{"path":"/admin/products/prod_01KD9XAGFNVGB24M98KWYZR4SV","status":400,"response_size":159}
```

**Critical Observations:**
1. `status: null` and `duration: null` on `/admin/uploads` - indicates upload request did NOT complete
2. Large request size: 29,534,328 bytes (~28MB)
3. Product save attempted AFTER incomplete upload → fails with 400
4. Images array contains items but `url` field is missing (never populated from S3)

### Environment Verification (Already Confirmed Working)
- ✅ S3 bucket configured: `tableclay-images`
- ✅ S3 region: `us-east-1`
- ✅ S3 file URL: `https://tableclay-images.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`
- ✅ S3 credentials present in Railway environment
- ✅ Middleware bodyParser limit: 25MB on `/admin/uploads`

### Investigation Tasks

#### 1. Check Railway Request Timeout
Railway has a default request timeout. Large uploads may exceed this.

**Check:**
```bash
# Via Railway dashboard or CLI
railway variables  # Look for timeout settings
```

**Reference:** Railway default timeout is typically 30 seconds for requests.

#### 2. Review S3 Upload Configuration
The S3 provider may have internal timeout settings.

**File to check:** `table-clay-store/medusa-config.ts`
```typescript
// Current S3 config (lines ~60-80)
{
  resolve: "@medusajs/medusa/file-s3",
  id: "s3",
  options: {
    file_url: process.env.S3_FILE_URL,
    access_key_id: process.env.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID,
    secret_access_key: process.env.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY,
    region: process.env.S3_REGION,
    bucket: process.env.S3_BUCKET,
  },
}
```

**Check for:** Missing timeout config, SDK version issues

#### 3. Test With Smaller Files
Determine if this is a timeout issue by testing file sizes:

**Test Matrix:**
| File Size | Expected Result |
|-----------|-----------------|
| < 1MB     | Should work     |
| 5MB       | Should work     |
| 10MB      | May timeout     |
| 25MB+     | Likely fails    |

#### 4. Check Medusa Core Upload Handler
Review how Medusa handles the upload endpoint.

**Files to trace:**
- `node_modules/@medusajs/medusa/dist/api/admin/uploads/route.js`
- S3 provider implementation

#### 5. Check Frontend Admin Dashboard
The admin dashboard may be triggering save before uploads complete.

**Hypothesis:** Race condition where:
1. User uploads images
2. Upload starts but takes time for large files
3. User clicks Save
4. Save request includes images array with pending uploads (no URLs yet)
5. Backend validates and fails because URLs are missing

### Diagnostic Commands

**Railway Logs (look for upload patterns):**
```bash
mcp__Railway__get-logs --logType deploy --lines 100 --filter "uploads"
```

**Test S3 Connection:**
```bash
# Test S3 bucket access
aws s3 ls s3://tableclay-images --region us-east-1
```

**Local Reproduction:**
```bash
cd table-clay-store
yarn dev
# Then upload large image in admin at localhost:9000/app
```

### Probable Root Causes (Ranked by Likelihood)

1. **Railway Request Timeout (70%)** - 28MB upload exceeds 30s timeout
2. **S3 SDK Timeout (20%)** - AWS SDK times out before completing upload
3. **Frontend Race Condition (10%)** - Dashboard sends save before upload completes

### Output Required
After investigation, document:
1. Exact cause of the failure
2. Which component is timing out
3. Recommended fix approach
4. Any configuration changes needed

### Files to Review
- `table-clay-store/medusa-config.ts` - S3 provider config
- `table-clay-store/src/api/middlewares.ts` - Upload middleware
- Railway service configuration
- Medusa admin dashboard source (node_modules)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause identified with evidence
- [ ] Timeout threshold determined (if applicable)
- [ ] Fix approach documented

title: BE-001: Google Places API Integration for Address Autocomplete
description:
## Project Context
Table Clay is a handmade pottery e-commerce store built on Medusa.js v2. This backend task supports the checkout overhaul by enabling address autocomplete.

## Overview
Integrate Google Places API to provide address autocomplete suggestions in the checkout delivery form.

## Why Server-Side Proxy?
- API key must NOT be exposed to client-side code
- Server endpoint proxies requests to Google Places API
- Adds security and allows rate limiting

## Requirements
1. Set up Google Places API key in backend environment
2. Create API endpoint to proxy Places requests
3. Return formatted address components

## Technical Details

### 1. Get Google Places API Key
1. Go to Google Cloud Console: https://console.cloud.google.com
2. Create or select a project
3. Enable 'Places API'
4. Create API credentials → API Key
5. Restrict key to Places API only (recommended)
6. Restrict by HTTP referrer or IP (recommended for production)

### 2. Environment Variables
```env
# table-clay-store/.env
GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY=AIzaSy...your_key_here
```

### 3. API Endpoints to Create

**Autocomplete endpoint:**
```
GET /store/address-autocomplete?input=123+main+st
```

**Place details endpoint:**
```
GET /store/address-autocomplete/details?place_id=ChIJ...
```

### 4. Implementation

Create: `table-clay-store/src/api/store/address-autocomplete/route.ts`

```typescript
import { MedusaRequest, MedusaResponse } from '@medusajs/framework'

export async function GET(req: MedusaRequest, res: MedusaResponse) {
  const { input } = req.query
  
  if (!input || typeof input !== 'string' || input.length < 3) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Input must be at least 3 characters' })
  }
  
  const apiKey = process.env.GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY
  if (!apiKey) {
    return res.status(500).json({ error: 'Places API not configured' })
  }
  
  try {
    const response = await fetch(
      `https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/place/autocomplete/json?input=${encodeURIComponent(input)}&types=address&components=country:us&key=${apiKey}`
    )
    const data = await response.json()
    
    // Transform to simpler format
    const suggestions = data.predictions.map((p: any) => ({
      place_id: p.place_id,
      description: p.description,
      structured: {
        main_text: p.structured_formatting.main_text,
        secondary_text: p.structured_formatting.secondary_text,
      }
    }))
    
    return res.json({ suggestions })
  } catch (error) {
    return res.status(500).json({ error: 'Failed to fetch suggestions' })
  }
}
```

```

### 5. Response Formats

**Autocomplete response:**
```typescript
interface AutocompleteResponse {
  suggestions: Array<{
    place_id: string
    description: string
    structured: {
      main_text: string
      secondary_text: string

description:
## Overview
Patch the Medusa admin dashboard's FileUpload component to increase the DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE from 1MB to 25MB. This requires using patch-package since the admin dashboard is part of Medusa core.

## Technical Background
The admin dashboard is compiled and distributed as part of `@medusajs/dashboard` package. The FileUpload component has a hardcoded constant:

```typescript
// Source: packages/admin/dashboard/src/components/common/file-upload/file-upload.tsx
const DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1024 * 1024  // 1MB
```

This constant is used as the default for the `maxFileSize` prop, which validates file sizes on the client side BEFORE uploading. Even if the backend allows 25MB, the frontend will reject files over 1MB.

## Solution: patch-package
We'll use `patch-package` to modify the compiled admin dashboard and persist the change across `yarn install`.

## Step-by-Step Implementation

### Step 1: Install patch-package (if not already installed)
```bash
cd table-clay-store
yarn add -D patch-package postinstall-postinstall
```

### Step 2: Find the file containing DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE
```bash
cd table-clay-store
grep -r "DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE" node_modules/@medusajs/dashboard/dist/
# OR
grep -r "1024.*1024" node_modules/@medusajs/dashboard/dist/*.mjs | head -20
```

The constant is likely in a chunk file like:
- `node_modules/@medusajs/dashboard/dist/chunk-XXXXXX.mjs`

### Step 3: Modify the file
Find the line that looks like:
```javascript
var DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1024 * 1024;
// or
const DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1048576;
// or minified version
var o=1048576
```

Change it to:
```javascript
var DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 25 * 1024 * 1024;
// or
const DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 26214400;
```

### Step 4: Create the patch
```bash
cd table-clay-store
npx patch-package @medusajs/dashboard
```

This creates: `patches/@medusajs+dashboard+X.X.X.patch`

### Step 5: Add postinstall script to package.json
Edit `table-clay-store/package.json`:
```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "postinstall": "patch-package"
  }
}
```

### Step 6: Commit the patch file
```bash
git add patches/
git commit -m "chore: Add patch for 25MB file upload limit"
```

## Alternative Approach (if patch-package is complex)
If the minified code is hard to patch, consider these alternatives:

### Option B: Environment Variable Override (Check if supported)
Check if Medusa supports runtime config for admin:
```bash
grep -r "MAX_FILE_SIZE" node_modules/@medusajs/dashboard/
```

### Option C: Custom Admin Route
Create a custom upload endpoint that bypasses the admin dashboard's validation. Less ideal but works.

## Verification
1. Run `yarn install` - patch should apply automatically
2. Start backend: `yarn dev`
3. Open admin at http://localhost:9000/app
4. Try uploading a 5MB image
5. File should NOT be rejected by frontend validation
6. File should upload successfully to S3

## What the Patch Should Look Like
```diff
diff --git a/node_modules/@medusajs/dashboard/dist/chunk-XXXXX.mjs b/node_modules/@medusajs/dashboard/dist/chunk-XXXXX.mjs
index abc123..def456 100644
--- a/node_modules/@medusajs/dashboard/dist/chunk-XXXXX.mjs
+++ b/node_modules/@medusajs/dashboard/dist/chunk-XXXXX.mjs
@@ -1234,7 +1234,7 @@
-var DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1048576;
+var DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_SIZE = 26214400;
```

## Risks
- **Medusa upgrades**: When upgrading @medusajs/dashboard, the patch may fail to apply. Re-create the patch after upgrades.
- **Minified code**: The variable name may be minified (e.g., `var a=1048576`). Search for the numeric value instead.

## Dependencies
- Requires TableClay-3ha (backend middleware) to be complete first
- Backend must accept 25MB or frontend fix is useless
close_reason: Created patches/@medusajs+dashboard+2.12.3.patch with 25MB file size limit

Send email notification when an order is shipped/fulfilled. Currently, customers only receive (or should receive) an order confirmation email. They have no notification when their order ships.

- Table Clay branded design (matching welcome/order confirmation emails)
- Order number (display_id)
- Tracking number (if available from fulfillment data)
- Carrier name (if available)
- Link to track shipment (if tracking URL available)
- Estimated delivery date (if available)

await notificationModuleService.createNotifications({
  to: order.email,
  channel: "email",
  content: {
    subject: "Your Table Clay order is on its way!",
    html: \`<!DOCTYPE html>...branded HTML...\`,
    text: \`Plain text version...\`,

})

title: FEATURE: Product Sales Tracking Module
description:
## Overview
Implement a backend module to track sales count per product. This enables data-driven 'bestseller' functionality for Related Products and admin analytics.

## Requirements
- Track total units sold per product (product level, not variant level)
- Increment count when order is placed (order.placed event) - NOT payment captured
- Do NOT decrement on order cancellation (once sold = sold)
- Display sales count in admin products list table (sortable column)
- Allow admin to manually edit sales_count for corrections/promotions
- Expose new API endpoint for storefront to fetch bestseller
- Initialize all existing products with sales_count = 0

## Technical Specifications

### 1. Database Model
Create new model in `table-clay-store/src/modules/sales-tracking/models/product-sales.ts`:
```typescript
@Entity()
export class ProductSales {
  @PrimaryColumn()
  product_id: string

  @Column({ type: 'int', default: 0 })
  sales_count: number

  @Column({ type: 'timestamp', nullable: true })
  last_sold_at: Date

  @UpdateDateColumn()
  updated_at: Date
}
```

### 2. Order Subscriber
File: `table-clay-store/src/subscribers/sales-tracker.ts`
```typescript
// Subscribe to: order.placed
// For each line item in order.items:
//   - Get product_id from variant
//   - Increment sales_count by item.quantity
//   - Update last_sold_at timestamp
// NOTE: Do NOT listen to order.canceled - counts stay
```

### 3. Store API Endpoint
File: `table-clay-store/src/api/store/products/bestseller/route.ts`
```typescript
// GET /store/products/bestseller?region_id=xxx
// Returns: Single product with highest sales_count
// Include: thumbnail, title, handle, calculated_price (for region)
// Cache: 5 minute TTL for performance
// Fallback: If no sales yet, return newest product
```

### 4. Admin API Extension
File: `table-clay-store/src/api/admin/products/[id]/sales/route.ts`
```typescript
// GET /admin/products/:id/sales - Get sales count
// PUT /admin/products/:id/sales - Update sales count (manual edit)
```

### 5. Admin UI Widget
File: `table-clay-store/src/admin/widgets/product-sales-column.tsx`
- Add 'Sales' column to products list table
- Column is sortable (click header to sort by sales)
- Click cell to edit value (inline editing)
- Format: number with locale formatting (e.g., '1,234')

## Files to Create/Modify
| File | Action | Purpose |
|------|--------|---------|
| `src/modules/sales-tracking/` | CREATE | New module directory |
| `src/modules/sales-tracking/models/product-sales.ts` | CREATE | Data model |
| `src/modules/sales-tracking/services/sales-tracker.ts` | CREATE | Business logic |
| `src/modules/sales-tracking/index.ts` | CREATE | Module entry point |
| `src/subscribers/sales-tracker.ts` | CREATE | Event handler |
| `src/api/store/products/bestseller/route.ts` | CREATE | Store API |
| `src/api/admin/products/[id]/sales/route.ts` | CREATE | Admin API |
| `src/admin/widgets/product-sales-column.tsx` | CREATE | Admin UI |
| `medusa-config.ts` | MODIFY | Register module |

## Database Migration
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS product_sales (
  product_id VARCHAR(255) PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES product(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  sales_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_sold_at TIMESTAMP,
  updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);
CREATE INDEX idx_product_sales_count ON product_sales(sales_count DESC);

-- Initialize existing products with 0 sales
INSERT INTO product_sales (product_id, sales_count)
SELECT id, 0 FROM product
ON CONFLICT (product_id) DO NOTHING;
```

## Testing Requirements
1. Unit test: Sales count increments correctly on order.placed
2. Unit test: Multiple quantities in one order increment by total quantity
3. Unit test: Bestseller endpoint returns highest sales product
4. Unit test: Admin can manually update sales count
5. Unit test: Cancellation does NOT decrement count
6. Integration test: Full order checkout flow updates sales

## Verification Steps
1. Deploy to Railway
2. Create test order via checkout
3. Verify sales_count incremented in database: `SELECT * FROM product_sales`
4. Verify admin products list shows Sales column
5. Edit a sales count in admin, verify persists
6. Call /store/products/bestseller, verify returns highest count product

## Dependencies
- Medusa v2.12.3 module system
- PostgreSQL for data storage
- No external services required

The `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_KEY` environment variable is EMPTY in:
1. Local: `table-clay-storefront/.env.local`
2. Production: Vercel environment (needs verification)

Without the publishable key, `loadStripe()` returns `null`, `StripeWrapper` never initializes, and `StripeContext` remains `false`, causing the skeleton fallback.

## Fix Steps
1. Get Stripe publishable key from [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/apikeys)
   - Live key starts with `pk_live_`
   - Test key starts with `pk_test_`
2. Add to `table-clay-storefront/.env.local`:
   ```
   NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_KEY=pk_live_YOUR_KEY_HERE
   ```
3. Add to Vercel production environment:
   ```bash
   vercel env add NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_KEY production
   ```
4. Redeploy storefront

## Files Involved
- `table-clay-storefront/.env.local` - Local env
- `table-clay-storefront/src/modules/checkout/components/payment-wrapper/index.tsx` - Loads Stripe
- `table-clay-storefront/src/modules/checkout/components/payment-form/index.tsx` - Uses StripeContext

## Verification
After fix, the checkout page should show the actual Stripe card input fields instead of gray skeleton placeholders.

Removed 'id: stripe' from the Stripe provider config in medusa-config.ts

The provider registration key formula is: pp_${identifier}${id ? _${id} : ''}
- With id: 'stripe' (WRONG) -> key = 'pp_stripe_stripe'
- Without id (CORRECT) -> key = 'pp_stripe'

The database had provider 'pp_stripe' linked to the region, but the container
was registering 'pp_stripe_stripe', causing the Awilix resolution failure.

## Context

Comprehensive testing across browsers and devices to ensure Express Checkout works correctly. This is the final verification step before the feature is considered complete.

**Blocked by:** EXP-008 (Product Actions Integration) - all implementation must be complete

### Klarna Testing

- [ ] Returns and completes order

---

## Test Scenarios

### 1. Happy Path
- [ ] Complete purchase with each payment method
- [ ] Verify order appears in Medusa Admin
- [ ] Verify customer receives confirmation email

### 2. Address Change Mid-Flow

## Test Cards

For Express Checkout in test mode, Stripe automatically handles test tokens. No special test cards are needed - wallet payments return test payment methods automatically.

For testing declined payments, use the standard Stripe test card numbers in the regular card form:

title: BE: Enable International Address Autocomplete
description:
Update the backend address autocomplete API to support international addresses instead of US-only.

## File to Modify
`table-clay-store/src/api/store/address-autocomplete/route.ts`

## Current Code (US-only, line 50-54):
```typescript
body: JSON.stringify({
  input,
  includedPrimaryTypes: ['street_address', 'premise', 'subpremise', 'route'],
  includedRegionCodes: ['us'], // Restrict to US addresses
}),
```

## Change Required:
Remove `includedRegionCodes: ['us']` to allow Google Places API to return addresses from any country:

```typescript
body: JSON.stringify({
  input,
  includedPrimaryTypes: ['street_address', 'premise', 'subpremise', 'route'],
  // No region restriction - supports international addresses
}),
```

## Why This Change
- Table Clay may ship internationally
- Address autocomplete should work for customers in any country
- The frontend already supports country selection dropdown

## Close Criteria
- [ ] Remove `includedRegionCodes: ['us']` from API request body
- [ ] Deploy backend to Railway
- [ ] Test: typing a UK address (e.g., '10 Downing Street') returns suggestions
- [ ] Test: typing a Canadian address returns suggestions
- [ ] Test: US addresses still work correctly
- [ ] Verify no errors in Railway logs after deploy
